newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine unions to meet Friday, consider strike.
newsitem.headline: Argentine unions to meet Friday, consider strike.

text.p: Argentina's top union leaders will meet Friday to consider their reactions to presidential decrees which have cut down union negotiating power in wage talks, a union official said Thursday.
He said leaders of the CGT labor federation will meet from 1000 local time (1300 GMT) to consider their options. Local media said earlier they would meet Thursday.
"The possibilities they will consider range from flooding the courts with legal actions to launching a strike," he told Reuters.
The official said unions Thursday consulted lawyers on the three decrees signed by President Carlos Menem late Wednesday after talks with unions ended in stalemate.

The measures allow workers to decide which union health scheme they sign up to and permit smaller firms to bypass national unions in collective wage talks with workers. Also, employers will now be able to appeal to the government if they want to negotiate with unions on a company-by-company and not an industry-wide basis.
Union anger at government moves to make labor markets more flexible and dilute the union health care monopoly led to a 36-hour general strike in September.
